newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks rally on Dow Jones, FOMC decision.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks rally on Dow Jones, FOMC decision.

text.p: Mexican stocks broke a six-day run of losses and regained the psychological 5,000 point mark at the close on Tuesday.
Dealers and analysts said bargain-hunters returned in the wake of gains on Wall Street and the Federal Open Market Committee decision to leave U.S. base rates unchanged.
"The fact U.S. rates did not change is what is bolstering the market," said Jose Gomez, an analyst at the Value brokerage.
The blue chip IPC share index .MXX soared 88.60 points, or 1.79 percent, at 5,041.48.
The Dow Jones industrial average rose 114.74 points to close at 7,918.10.
Gomez said investor confidence had gradually returned to the bourse after the recent slew of losses had made prices ripe for bargain hunters.
"The fact that prices fell so sharply made them attractive, especially for short-term investors...The market is recouping lost ground and we can see that in improving volume," he said.
Volume .TV.MX was moderate at 96.7 million shares, but much heavier than Monday's dismal total.
Market heavyweight Telefonos de Mexico set the pace, dealers said, gaining 20 centavos to 20.40 pesos. The telecomms firm's ADRs ended up 15/16 at 52-1/2.
Traders said financial groups gained sharply after the FOMC decision as investors looked forward to lower interest rates at home and a consequent improvement in loan quality.
Bancomer, one of Mexico's biggest financial groups, ended up 22 centavos at 5.46 pesos.
Glassmaker Vitro was a prominent gainer, rising 1.40 pesos to 36.40 on Monday's late news it had formed a $100 million joint venture with Libbey Inc, dealers said.

Television network TV Azteca fell 1.37 pesos to 35.43, the price at which it went public on Friday, while its rival Televisa gained 4.00 pesos to 127.00 on news it would issue $1.6 billion in commercial paper, dealers said.
On the broad market, gainers trounced decliners by 70 to 25, out of 119 stocks traded in total.
